::: {.callout-note}
This page presents retained ideal reference evidence. It does not define an
active ePC-SAFT parameter set and does not rerun the generators during a site
build.
:::

## Ownership and question

This analysis owns the curated ideal pressure and ideal-activity speciation
tables and figures. It asks how the source-controlled reaction system compares
with the retained pressure and speciation observations over the canonical
temperature and loading coordinates.

The six-species calculation remains owned by
`analyses/six_species_solubility_reference/`, and the neutral parity
calculation remains owned by `analyses/neutral_pcsaft_pressure_reference/`.
This page summarizes their evidence and keeps the manuscript presentation in
one place; it does not duplicate or adopt their result ownership.

## Retained results

The ideal pressure table contains 31 observations for both the legacy
Smith–Missen and neutral reference lanes. Their overall median absolute
log10 errors are 0.1601 and 0.1601, respectively; the retained rows are
numerically equivalent within the source/reference precision documented in the
result tables.

The ideal speciation outputs cover the canonical comparison rows and report
species-level log10 residual metrics, including the combined MEA + MEAH⁺ and
carbamate partitions. The retained claim boundary and residual audit are the
authority for interpretation:

- [claim boundary](results/ideal_reference_claim_boundary.md)
- [model lineage](results/ideal_reference_model_lineage.md)
- [pressure metrics](results/ideal_reference_pressure_metrics.csv)
- [speciation metrics](results/ideal_reference_speciation_metrics.csv)
- [pressure results](results/ideal_reference_pressure_results.csv)
- [speciation results](results/ideal_reference_speciation_results.csv)

## Reproduce or render

Numerical generation and figure rendering remain separate from this disabled
documentation page:

```bash
uv run python analyses/ideal_reaction_equilibrium/scripts/generate_data.py
uv run python analyses/ideal_reaction_equilibrium/scripts/render_figures.py
```
